questions.title: What evidence can be considered under Rule 12(b)(6) for copyright fair use claims?
questions.question_body: The Second Circuit states it can look at 'facts alleged in the complaint, documents attached... and documents incorporated by reference.' But does this include judicial notice of copyright registrations? Is it fair use a substantive case or a procedural pleading issue, and what standard of proof applies at this stage?

questions.title: Why is the subjective intent of the user irrelevant for transformative use?
questions.question_body: Under Section 107, the court cites *Andy Warhol Found.* regarding 'purpose and character' of the use. Does the court mean that the 'purpose' is determined by an external observer, not the copyright holder? How does this align with Kimmel's argument that he initiated the creation?

questions.title: Why restrict fair use market harm to 'competing substitutes' rather than 'commercial damage'?
questions.question_body: The court cites *Hachette Book* saying 'we ask not whether the second work would damage the market... but whether it usurps the market.' Why does the Fourth Factor focus on market substitution and not just harm caused by parody or criticism?

questions.title: Does *Harper & Row* mean 'bad faith' automatically bars fair use?
questions.question_body: The opinion quotes *Harper & Row* that 'fair use presupposes good faith.' But it also says the Second Circuit has 'distanced itself' from this interpretation. So, if Kimmel used bad faith motives regarding false representations, does that invalidate the fair use defense?

questions.title: Why avoid ruling on preemption claims when a claim fails on its own merits?
questions.question_body: The court states it 'needs not resolve' the argument about whether the state law claims were preempted by the Copyright Act, choosing instead to dismiss them because they 'failed to state a claim.' What is the procedural significance of saving preemption for the state court vs dismissing on the pleadings?

questions.title: Why is the Illinois presumption against third parties relevant when suing under the Terms of Service?
questions.question_body: Under Illinois law, the court presumes against benefits to noncontracting third parties without an 'express declaration.' How does this interact with the allegation that Kimmel must have agreed to the Terms of Service as a user to sue as a third-party beneficiary?

questions.title: What is the specific injury requirement for fraudulent inducement under NY law?
questions.question_body: The court affirms the dismissal for failure to allege 'out-of-pocket loss' as required under *Lama Holding Co.* or *Connaughton*. Is this strictly a New York requirement for contract damages, and why does the lack of specific loss lead to a failure to state a claim?
